Multnomah County Circuit Court No. 20CR10244
Court of Appeals No. A186194
ORDER REMANDING FOR RESENTENCING; APPELLATE JUDGMENT
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
The parties jointly move under ORAP 10.35 to remand the judgment on appeal
for resentencing.1 Specifically, the parties agree that the trial court erred by imposing
consecutive sentences and per diem fees, when neither of those terms were announced
in defendant’s presence at sentencing. See State v. Schay-Vivero, 333 Or App 168,
169, 552 P3d 150 (2024); State v. Priester, 325 Or App 574, 581, 530 P3d 118, rev den,
371 Or 332 (2023). The motion is granted.
The parties agree that the appeal does not present a substantial question of law.
They also agree on the disposition of the appeal and that a published opinion would not
benefit the bench, the bar, or the public. The court agrees with the parties’ identification
of error and that summary disposition is appropriate in this case.
Remanded for resentencing; otherwise affirmed.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
6/15/2026
1 A copy of the parties’ motion, for the trial court’s review, is available on the
court’s Appellate Case Management System (ACMS).
